candidates.summary: Pope Leo XIV underwent surgery that confirmed lung adenocarcinoma, and doctors removed the lower lobe of his right lung. The Vatican said the operation was successful and that decisions about chemotherapy or other treatment would await additional test results, including whether the cancer had spread to lymph nodes.
candidates.title: Pope Leo diagnosed with lung cancer after surgery

candidates.summary: Congo's Health Ministry reported 9,066 confirmed Ebola cases and 4,381 deaths, with 88 new cases in its latest report. The outbreak had spread across 65 health zones in seven provinces, and officials said many infections remained undetected while community transmission continued.
candidates.title: Congo's Ebola outbreak surpasses 9,000 confirmed cases

candidates.summary: The U.S. Treasury announced more than $1.21 billion in penalties against Bank of America for anti-money-laundering and sanctions violations. Treasury said the bank failed to report more than $5 billion in suspicious transactions on time. Bank of America admitted willfully violating the Bank Secrecy Act and said it was addressing the compliance failures.
candidates.title: US imposes more than $1.21 billion in penalties on Bank of America

candidates.summary: The Justice Department unsealed a complaint charging OpenAI engineer Abdulrahman Alfozan with attempting to intercept oral communications using a concealed recording device in an executive conference room. The Saudi national was arrested October 9 and appeared in federal court Tuesday. The complaint's allegations have not been proven in court.
candidates.title: OpenAI employee charged over hidden recording device

candidates.summary: The U.S. Justice Department announced charges against 14 people and the arrests of two Americans accused of supporting North Korean remote-worker schemes. Authorities said operations targeting more than 40 suspected Texas "laptop farms" seized approximately 187 devices. The alleged schemes affected more than 70 U.S. companies and generated at least $3 million for overseas workers.
candidates.title: US announces crackdown on North Korean remote-worker schemes

candidates.summary: AT&T agreed to sell its Mexican wireless business to Grupo Televisa and Fintech Holdings for $2 billion in cash, subject to adjustments and regulatory approval. The companies expect the transaction to close in the first quarter of 2027; AT&T said the pending divestiture would sharpen its focus on U.S. fiber and 5G investment.
candidates.title: AT&T agrees to sell Mexico unit for $2 billion
